description: DIN rail 3-phase power network meter with harmonics up to 63, two alarm relays, data logging and Ethernet; Modbus RTU over RS485 and Modbus TCP

sources.title: NR30 user's manual (NR30-09E_R1)
sources.note: section 12, tables 15-22 and the quantity tables

source: Lumel, NR30 user's manual NR30-09E_R1, section 12
notes: Measurements are read from the 8000 area: IEEE 754 floats in two registers, byte order 3-2-1-0 (high word first). The same values are at 6000 (order 1-0-3-2) and as 32-bit registers at 7500-7985.
Harmonics 2-51 are in the 8000 area and harmonics 52-63 in the 9200 area (order 3-2-1-0); the 9000 area has the same values in order 1-0-3-2.
Which values exist depends on the connection type (3Ph/4W, 3Ph/3W, 1Ph/2W); in 3Ph/3W the per-phase powers, voltages and power factors are not available.

Energy is available as floats (an overflow count in 100 MWh and a counter in kWh, kvarh or kVAh) and as 32-bit integers in hundredths of kWh. The 24-hour exported energy row is printed in the manual with the address of an earlier row; here it follows the pattern of the other rows (overflows 7991, counter 7992).
The Modbus TCP service uses the same register map (port 502 by default, device address in register 4146).
The Modbus map of the ND30 has the same layout but differs in the configuration and display registers, so it is not covered by this file.
